title: Monitor childcare fees and review costs and profits every three years
action: Instead of relying on fee caps tied to wage funding, monitor fee rises and out-of-pocket costs, investigate services whose fees move out of step with similar services, and hold a three-yearly review of fees, costs and profits.
why: Monitoring keeps pressure on fees while letting providers respond to costs and demand; fixed caps can discourage new services and expansion where they are most needed.

evidence.source: A path to universal early childhood education and care (volume 1)
evidence.quote: The Australian Government should continue to monitor changes in ECEC fees and out-of-pocket expenses on a regular basis to identify services where movements are out of step with sector norms.

evidence.source: A path to universal early childhood education and care (volume 1)
evidence.quote: Increases in fees that vary markedly from those of similar services should prompt closer investigation, and a regulatory response should be considered if they are not reasonable.
